## Where this fits

This is the **required core artifact** for Assignment 7. The Shiny exemplar
shown in class is a demonstration only; adapt this Quarto file instead.

## Goal

This starter shows how to turn the Week 7 descriptive summary into a dashboard-style KT product. It uses one editable control value, one visualization, one table, one interpretation, and one caution — the 1-1-1-1-1 rule made concrete.

## Audience Question

Audience: A health anthropologist studying socioeconomic inequalities and how that realtes to health patterns/and or outcomes among the adult populaiton, specifcally looking at low income groups. 

Question: How has average BMI levels changed over time within adults in the low income group?  What insights might be uncovered in regards to socioecomic health inequalites? 
## Setup

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)  # AI-EDIT(2026-06-23): tidyverse-default — consolidated core library() calls into library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

```

## Control

For this dashboard I selected low income groups to explore how average BMI has changed over time among adults with fewer finical resources compared to those in other groups. 

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-control
available_income_groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(nhanes$IncomeGroup)))
selected_income <- "Low Income (<1.3)"
#"High Income (>3.5)" this was for when i rendered checked with high income. kept as a comment. 
if (!selected_income %in% available_income_groups) {
  selected_income <- available_income_groups[1]
}

selected_income
```


## Summary

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-summary
dashboard_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    IncomeGroup == selected_income,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(dashboard_summary)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot
ggplot(dashboard_summary, aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "#2f6f73") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, color = "#2f6f73") +
  labs(
    title = paste("BMI Trends Over Time:", selected_income),
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset",
    x = "Survey period (NHANES cycle)",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    caption = "Descriptive, unweighted classroom summary. Missing BMI, income group, cycle, and out-of-cohort ages are excluded."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Interpretation

The dashboard shows that mean BMI among low income adults increased from 28.8 in 1999–2000 to 30.4 in 2021–2023, with some fluctuations across survey cycles. From a health anthropology perspective, these patterns raise questions about how socioeconomic conditions and access to resources may influence health outcomes. However, the dashboard cannot determine the causes of these changes.


## Limitation
This dashboard cannot establish whether income causes changes in BMI or represent national population trends. This is because the analysis uses unweighted descriptive data, the findings cannot be generalized to the national population.

## To Note (Assignment): 

## Privacy-Safe Publishing

- Use aggregate summaries, not row-level records.
- Avoid small-cell interpretations when `n` is low.
- State that outputs are descriptive and unweighted.
- Keep cached classroom data separate from any raw NHANES retrieval workflow.
- Do not upload row-level data to external AI tools.
